currentContext.expansion: FY26 was a year of significant footprint expansion. In line with its growth strategy the Company grew its total number of centres to 76 and added capacity of 17,288 desks, taking total operational desk capacity to over 1,26,860 desks; operational area rose to 8.6 MSF while Area Under Management (operational area plus signed leases and signed letters of intent) stood at 11.6 MSF, which management says gives visibility on long-term growth. The expansion was undertaken across key markets with a focus on strengthening the Company's presence in existing micro-markets and addressing growing customer demand for high-quality flexible workspace solutions, with centres spread across eight cities. Capital expenditure during the year went towards the expansion of additional centres and operational area, and the addition of new centres also drove the growth in property, plant and equipment and right-of-use assets, in common area maintenance and housekeeping costs, and in lease liabilities; investing outflow rose on increased investment in new centres. Growth was funded largely from operating cash flows, with the Company remaining net-debt-negative. Alongside physical footprint, the Company built out platform capacity: the workforce increased from 552 to 578 employees as at 31 March 2026, primarily to support business growth and strengthen the technology and engineering team in line with its focus on product and technological innovation; Managed Office was scaled into a standalone growth engine; Rivet, the in-house design and build capability, was extended to external clients; and the WeWork India app brought the member network onto a single digital layer. The other milestone of the year was the completion of the Initial Public Offering, comprising an Offer for Sale of 4,62,96,296 equity shares, with the equity shares listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited with effect from October 10, 2025. On an IGAAP-equivalent basis, revenue growth was attributed to portfolio expansion, mature centre occupancy gains and sustained momentum in Value-Added Services and Managed Office solutions.

risks.note: A substantial portion of demand depends on global corporate spending cycles and the cyclical dynamics of the sectors served - including technology, which accounts for a significant share of demand across the flexible workspace industry. Market slowdowns and geopolitical uncertainty may affect trade and capital flows, and sector-specific downturns could defer leasing decisions and hit occupancy and pricing. Mitigated by a diversified member base with no sector dominant, an approximately 65% global / 35% domestic occupier mix, longer-tenor commitments and a forward order book.

risks.risk: Project execution and delivery of new centres
risks.note: Growth depends on the timely development, fit-out and operationalisation of new centres; delays from landlord handovers, design finalisation, procurement, vendor performance or construction can postpone openings, escalate project costs, delay revenue and damage member experience and reputation. Mitigated by a project governance framework backed by a track record of 76+ delivered centres, pre-finalisation technical due diligence, empanelled vendors, contractual handover conditions and independent technical certification before a centre goes operational.

risks.risk: Lease renewal risk on a fully leased portfolio
risks.note: Centres operate under long-term leases with landlords that must be renegotiated at term end, and some leases may not renew on terms consistent with expectations. Mitigated by long-standing developer relationships giving early visibility of renewal timelines, portfolio-level rather than deal-by-deal negotiation, a staggered lease maturity profile, a landlord base diversified across cities and micro-markets, and the option to relocate operations to alternative assets in the same market.

The industry faces increasing competition from established operators, new entrants and real estate developers offering managed office and flexible workspace solutions; intensifying competition, evolving customer preferences, technological change and pricing pressure may affect market share, member acquisition and retention and the ability to sustain profitability. Mitigated by continuous investment in portfolio, product, brand and market intelligence, 11.6 Million square feet of committed Grade A AUM across eight Tier-1 cities, one of the widest product portfolios in the Indian flex market and dedicated commercial teams tracking competitor and pricing dynamics.

risks.risk: Absorption outpacing new Grade A supply
risks.note: Grade A office absorption in India has consistently outpaced new construction through the current cycle; while tighter supply favours established operators in premium micro-markets, it can pressure lease terms on new take-ups and extend deal timelines for expansion into new micro-markets. Mitigated by an 18-24 month forward pipeline of 11.6 MSF AUM already secured through signed leases and LOIs, portfolio-level relationships with all major landlords and market intelligence tools that allow anchor tenant positions to be taken two to three years before completion.

The Company relies extensively on digital platforms; its digital check-in system, member apps and smart-building IoT infrastructure collect personally identifiable information including names, phone numbers and email addresses of members and visitors, and data breaches carry statutory penalties under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA), 2023 as well as significant reputational risk.

risks.risk: Regulatory, policy and multi-state compliance exposure
risks.note: Regulatory or policy changes in commercial real estate, labour and taxation could affect the cost base, operating model or expansion economics, and as a listed entity operating across multiple states the Company is subject to local, state and national regulation spanning labour, environment, fire safety, taxation, anti-bribery and corruption and securities law; non-compliance creates direct financial exposure through penalties and litigation plus reputational risk. Mitigated by a dedicated compliance function, a mapped compliance management system, quarterly compliance reports to the Board, half-yearly Risk Management Committee review, third-party audits and mandatory employee training.

Structural concentration disclosed in the BRSR: 98.00% of turnover comes from a single activity - renting and operating of office buildings and coworking spaces - and the Company operates exclusively within the domestic Indian market with nil export revenue, so the entire earnings base is levered to one product category in one country. Permanent employee turnover of 23.50% in FY26 adds a people-continuity dimension to a service business dependent on consistent member experience.

risks.risk: Occupant health and safety across a large member base
risks.note: Serving a large and diverse member base across all locations exposes operations to physical safety risks (fire, slips, infrastructure hazards), health risks (ergonomics, indoor environmental quality) and regulatory obligations under ISO 45001 and local safety regulations; failure can impact business continuity, legal compliance, member trust and brand reputation.

risks.risk: Energy intensity, climate transition and GHG emissions
risks.note: Flexible workspaces are energy-intensive - HVAC, lighting and IT infrastructure operate continuously across 70+ locations - so high energy consumption directly drives Scope 1 and 2 emissions and inflates operating costs, amplified by India's grid carbon intensity remaining among the highest globally. As a listed entity in a carbon-intensive sector the Company also faces regulatory, reputational and transition risks as investors and ESG rating agencies expect transparent GHG accounting, science-aligned targets and climate risk disclosure under evolving SEBI norms.

one-line thesis: Growth-cycle quarter that must be read YoY, not QoQ: revenue Rs 698 cr (+28.5% YoY), EBITDA Rs 138 cr (+69%, 19.8% margin), PAT Rs 53.2 cr (~6.5x), net debt down ~90% to Rs 31.6 cr. India's largest branded flex network is front-loading capex (Rs 188 cr in Q1) into a market where flex is taking record office-leasing share; management guides 20%+ FY27 revenue/EBITDA growth and Rs 500-600 cr capex, and just launched a Member Services marketplace as a pure-margin optionality layer.

Centre-level EBITDA dip (Rs 212→186 cr) fully explained by Rs 37 cr higher customization last quarter. FCFF −Rs 46.1 cr (growth-intensive H1; FCFO +176% to Rs 141.9 cr).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue & EBITDA growth:** "definitely meet" 20%+ for FY27 (pre-Ind-AS basis referenced); base to rise each quarter.
- **EBITDA margin:** 19-20% to hold through expansion and expand as occupancy ramps (Q2 additions skew to managed office → margin-accretive).
- **Capex:** Rs 500-600 cr for FY27 (reaffirmed); upside only if large managed-office deals require extra fit-out capex (visibility by next quarter).
- **Capacity:** by **March 2027 → ~10.3 mn sq ft, ~155,000 desks**; H1 FY27 adds ~22,000 desks (~20,000 seats opening by October, ~6,000 managed office). FY28 → ~12 mn sq ft (similar growth pace, already in negotiation).
- **Customization revenue:** run-rate Rs 10-15 cr/quarter going forward (large managed-office customization now amortised over contract term to kill lumpiness).
- **Revenue mix:** VAS ~11-12% + digital ~3-4% ≈ 16% of revenue, held steady.
- **Promoter pledge / debt:** endeavour to remove/pay off the ~Rs 570 cr pledged debt within FY27 (asset sale in parent or a block); ~30 lakh shares to be released next quarter (currently ~15% pledged).
order book & pipeline: 79 centres / 8 cities / 9.1 mn sq ft / 133.6k desks; +11 centres & ~20k desks YoY (+18.5%). Contracted capacity ~12 mn sq ft / ~179,000 desks (32% capacity growth, ~44k desks locked in). Sold ~12,700 desks in Q1 (+28% YoY; April biggest-ever month at ~7,500, no discounting). Visibility: ~100% at 12 months, ~90% at 18 months, ~80% at 24 months. Occupancy 84.9% (mature 87.5%, growth centres ~65% — above 56.6% break-even); NPS +78.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Core workspace** Rs 603 cr (+30%), the engine; 77% revenue from enterprise, 65% global companies, 46% North-America GCC-driven; top-10 members just 22% of revenue (no concentration). Tech 28%, BFSI 17%.
- **VAS** +10% (parking/facilities/customization/late fees); ex-customization +20% QoQ.
- **Digital** Rs 26 cr (+27% YoY, +22% QoQ), <4% of revenue but ~80% EBITDA margin — monetises the same sq ft more than once.
- **Rivet** — nascent; some pipeline, revenue building over next 3 quarters; ~10-15% margin, full flow-through to PAT.
- **Member Services** — launched 15 Jul 2026; in-app B2B marketplace (admin/IT, HR, GCC setup; legal/marketing/sustainability to follow); listing fee + 6-16% take rate; structured as pure-margin/e-commerce (mostly flows to margin, not top line).
growth verticals / optionality: Managed office (build-to-suit; Q2 skew ~7,000 managed seats, margin-accretive) as the operator-vs-REIT moat play; Member Services (larger share of member wallet — transport/hiring/insurance); Digital stack; Rivet. GCC/enterprise demand (North America 46% of revenue) is the core secular driver.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Scale + brand:** largest branded flex network in India, concentrated in the 8 fastest-growing enterprise/GCC micro-markets; flex share of office leasing >doubled in 5 quarters to 27%, ~55% of occupiers already use flex (targeting ~two-thirds by 2027).
- **Sticky base / low CAC:** 52% of desk sales from existing members, 84% renewals; every Re 1 of new rent added Rs 4.7 of contracted revenue.
- **Operator moat vs REITs:** customers want one partner across multiple formats/cities (e.g., Amazon: WeWork seats in Bangalore + Pune + managed office in Chennai) plus full FM/experience layer REITs won't run; WeWork offers 3-5 yr flexibility vs REIT 9-yr lock, absorbing re-lease risk (revenue-to-rent 2.9-3x).
- **Operating leverage:** rent/sq ft flat YoY, opex/sq ft +5.6% vs revenue +28%; break-even occupancy only 56.6%.
margins & cost dynamics: Company EBITDA margin 19.8% (target 19-20% hold, then expand as ~22k H1 desks ramp post-October). Southern markets (Hyderabad/Chennai, managed-office-heavy) carry higher spread (2.8-3x+) but lower price; premium micro-markets (Delhi Aerocity, Rs 25-35k/desk) higher price, lower spread — revenue-to-rent held 2.9-3x overall. Customization is ~full flow-through (no COGS/rent). Brokerage & large-customization now amortised over contract term (cash upfront, P&L smoothed).
capex / expansion (watch slippage): FY27 capex Rs 500-600 cr; Rs 188 cr spent in Q1. ~20,000 seats opening by October (some slipped ~1-2 weeks from Q1 into July on customer design changes / better openings). March-2027 target 10.3 mn sq ft / 155k desks; FY28 ~12 mn sq ft. Deliberately avoids over-committing supply far in advance to retain agility. Regular refurb at year 6-7 (~5-10% of initial capex).
capital allocation: Deleveraging story: net debt Rs 31.6 cr (0.06x EBITDA), CoB down to 8.5%, rating A+. IPO (Oct 2025) raised ~Rs 3,000 cr vs planned Rs 4,000 cr → left a ~Rs 570 cr debt stub, source of the ~15% promoter pledge; management targets full payoff within FY27 (asset sale or block). Capex self-funded by operations (FCFO +176%).
risks & watch-items:
- Growth-cycle margin/FCFF volatility — heavy H1 capex, FCFF −Rs 46 cr; thesis depends on H2 occupancy ramp flowing through.
- Customization-revenue lumpiness now masked by amortisation — watch reported vs cash divergence.
- Promoter pledge (~15%) until the Rs 570 cr stub is cleared — execution risk on the FY27 payoff.
- REIT competition in managed/build-to-suit (management's rebuttal: FM + flexibility + multi-format relationship).
- Concentration in enterprise/GCC/North-America demand — sensitive to global GCC capex cycles.
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined framing ("read us YoY, not QoQ"; growth costs arrive before revenue). Proactive and specific on customization accounting change, pledge-reduction plan, and per-market margin math. Committed language on shareholder returns and FY27/FY28 momentum.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The accounting change (amortising large managed-office customization) structurally smooths revenue — future QoQ comps get cleaner but headline customization drops to Rs 10-15 cr/qtr.
- Member Services is engineered as pure-margin (mostly booked as margin, not top line) — will lift EBITDA% without proportionate revenue, distorting margin reads upward.
- Contracted revenue (Rs 3,363 cr) growing 2x faster than contracted rent is the clearest forward-visibility signal — Rs 4.7 revenue per Re 1 new rent.
- Q2 additions skew to pre-sold managed office → management expects margin UP despite heavy openings (opposite of last year's expansion dip).

one-line thesis: Growth-cycle quarter that must be read YoY, not QoQ: revenue Rs 698 cr (+28.5% YoY), EBITDA Rs 138 cr (+69%, 19.8% margin), PAT Rs 53.2 cr (~6.5x), net debt down ~90% to Rs 31.6 cr. India's largest branded flex network is front-loading capex (Rs 188 cr in Q1) into a market where flex is taking record office-leasing share; management guides 20%+ FY27 revenue/EBITDA growth and Rs 500-600 cr capex, and just launched a Member Services marketplace as a pure-margin optionality layer.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1 FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (total) | Rs 698 cr | +28.5% | Rev from ops Rs 687 cr (+28%); core workspace Rs 603 cr (+30%), VAS +10%, digital Rs 26 cr (+27%) |
| EBITDA / margin | Rs 138.3 cr / 19.8% | +69% (margin 15%→19.8%) | Centre-level EBITDA Rs 186 cr / 27.8% (+52%) |
| PAT | Rs 53.2 cr | vs Rs 8.4 cr (~6.5x) | PAT margin 1.5%→7.6% |
| ROCE | 28.6% | vs 9.1% (~3x) | |
| Cash / net debt | Net debt Rs 31.6 cr (−89% from Rs 297 cr) | | Cash Rs 371 cr; net-debt/EBITDA 0.06x; CoB 10.4%→8.5%; rating A-→A+ |
| Contracted future revenue | Rs 3,363 cr | +60% (from Rs 2,105 cr) | Locked-in member revenue over ~27-mth avg; rent obligations grew only 30% |
> QoQ optics distorted by Q4 FY26's one-time customization revenue (Rs 47 cr → Rs 9.5 cr this qtr) and by front-loaded expansion capex. Centre-level EBITDA dip (Rs 212→186 cr) fully explained by Rs 37 cr higher customization last quarter. FCFF −Rs 46.1 cr (growth-intensive H1; FCFO +176% to Rs 141.9 cr).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue & EBITDA growth:** "definitely meet" 20%+ for FY27 (pre-Ind-AS basis referenced); base to rise each quarter.
- **EBITDA margin:** 19-20% to hold through expansion and expand as occupancy ramps (Q2 additions skew to managed office → margin-accretive).
- **Capex:** Rs 500-600 cr for FY27 (reaffirmed); upside only if large managed-office deals require extra fit-out capex (visibility by next quarter).
- **Capacity:** by **March 2027 → ~10.3 mn sq ft, ~155,000 desks**; H1 FY27 adds ~22,000 desks (~20,000 seats opening by October, ~6,000 managed office). FY28 → ~12 mn sq ft (similar growth pace, already in negotiation).
- **Customization revenue:** run-rate Rs 10-15 cr/quarter going forward (large managed-office customization now amortised over contract term to kill lumpiness).
- **Revenue mix:** VAS ~11-12% + digital ~3-4% ≈ 16% of revenue, held steady.
- **Promoter pledge / debt:** endeavour to remove/pay off the ~Rs 570 cr pledged debt within FY27 (asset sale in parent or a block); ~30 lakh shares to be released next quarter (currently ~15% pledged).
order book & pipeline: 79 centres / 8 cities / 9.1 mn sq ft / 133.6k desks; +11 centres & ~20k desks YoY (+18.5%). Contracted capacity ~12 mn sq ft / ~179,000 desks (32% capacity growth, ~44k desks locked in). Sold ~12,700 desks in Q1 (+28% YoY; April biggest-ever month at ~7,500, no discounting). Visibility: ~100% at 12 months, ~90% at 18 months, ~80% at 24 months. Occupancy 84.9% (mature 87.5%, growth centres ~65% — above 56.6% break-even); NPS +78.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Core workspace** Rs 603 cr (+30%), the engine; 77% revenue from enterprise, 65% global companies, 46% North-America GCC-driven; top-10 members just 22% of revenue (no concentration). Tech 28%, BFSI 17%.
- **VAS** +10% (parking/facilities/customization/late fees); ex-customization +20% QoQ.
- **Digital** Rs 26 cr (+27% YoY, +22% QoQ), <4% of revenue but ~80% EBITDA margin — monetises the same sq ft more than once.
- **Rivet** — nascent; some pipeline, revenue building over next 3 quarters; ~10-15% margin, full flow-through to PAT.
- **Member Services** — launched 15 Jul 2026; in-app B2B marketplace (admin/IT, HR, GCC setup; legal/marketing/sustainability to follow); listing fee + 6-16% take rate; structured as pure-margin/e-commerce (mostly flows to margin, not top line).
growth verticals / optionality: Managed office (build-to-suit; Q2 skew ~7,000 managed seats, margin-accretive) as the operator-vs-REIT moat play; Member Services (larger share of member wallet — transport/hiring/insurance); Digital stack; Rivet. GCC/enterprise demand (North America 46% of revenue) is the core secular driver.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Scale + brand:** largest branded flex network in India, concentrated in the 8 fastest-growing enterprise/GCC micro-markets; flex share of office leasing >doubled in 5 quarters to 27%, ~55% of occupiers already use flex (targeting ~two-thirds by 2027).
- **Sticky base / low CAC:** 52% of desk sales from existing members, 84% renewals; every Re 1 of new rent added Rs 4.7 of contracted revenue.
- **Operator moat vs REITs:** customers want one partner across multiple formats/cities (e.g., Amazon: WeWork seats in Bangalore + Pune + managed office in Chennai) plus full FM/experience layer REITs won't run; WeWork offers 3-5 yr flexibility vs REIT 9-yr lock, absorbing re-lease risk (revenue-to-rent 2.9-3x).
- **Operating leverage:** rent/sq ft flat YoY, opex/sq ft +5.6% vs revenue +28%; break-even occupancy only 56.6%.
margins & cost dynamics: Company EBITDA margin 19.8% (target 19-20% hold, then expand as ~22k H1 desks ramp post-October). Southern markets (Hyderabad/Chennai, managed-office-heavy) carry higher spread (2.8-3x+) but lower price; premium micro-markets (Delhi Aerocity, Rs 25-35k/desk) higher price, lower spread — revenue-to-rent held 2.9-3x overall. Customization is ~full flow-through (no COGS/rent). Brokerage & large-customization now amortised over contract term (cash upfront, P&L smoothed).
capex / expansion (watch slippage): FY27 capex Rs 500-600 cr; Rs 188 cr spent in Q1. ~20,000 seats opening by October (some slipped ~1-2 weeks from Q1 into July on customer design changes / better openings). March-2027 target 10.3 mn sq ft / 155k desks; FY28 ~12 mn sq ft. Deliberately avoids over-committing supply far in advance to retain agility. Regular refurb at year 6-7 (~5-10% of initial capex).
capital allocation: Deleveraging story: net debt Rs 31.6 cr (0.06x EBITDA), CoB down to 8.5%, rating A+. IPO (Oct 2025) raised ~Rs 3,000 cr vs planned Rs 4,000 cr → left a ~Rs 570 cr debt stub, source of the ~15% promoter pledge; management targets full payoff within FY27 (asset sale or block). Capex self-funded by operations (FCFO +176%).
risks & watch-items:
- Growth-cycle margin/FCFF volatility — heavy H1 capex, FCFF −Rs 46 cr; thesis depends on H2 occupancy ramp flowing through.
- Customization-revenue lumpiness now masked by amortisation — watch reported vs cash divergence.
- Promoter pledge (~15%) until the Rs 570 cr stub is cleared — execution risk on the FY27 payoff.
- REIT competition in managed/build-to-suit (management's rebuttal: FM + flexibility + multi-format relationship).
- Concentration in enterprise/GCC/North-America demand — sensitive to global GCC capex cycles.
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined framing ("read us YoY, not QoQ"; growth costs arrive before revenue). Proactive and specific on customization accounting change, pledge-reduction plan, and per-market margin math. Committed language on shareholder returns and FY27/FY28 momentum.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The accounting change (amortising large managed-office customization) structurally smooths revenue — future QoQ comps get cleaner but headline customization drops to Rs 10-15 cr/qtr.
- Member Services is engineered as pure-margin (mostly booked as margin, not top line) — will lift EBITDA% without proportionate revenue, distorting margin reads upward.
- Contracted revenue (Rs 3,363 cr) growing 2x faster than contracted rent is the clearest forward-visibility signal — Rs 4.7 revenue per Re 1 new rent.
- Q2 additions skew to pre-sold managed office → management expects margin UP despite heavy openings (opposite of last year's expansion dip).

themes.title: Flexible workspace, PropTech & commercial real-estate services
themes.need: The GCC build-out and hybrid-work shift drive managed/flexible office demand, and Q1FY27 showed flex becoming the marginal buyer of Indian office space. SMARTWORKS grew revenue 44% to INR 546cr with normalized EBITDA INR 107cr (+74%) at a 19.6% margin, lifted GCC clients from 15% to 21% of revenue in a single quarter, and reported India's highest-ever quarterly leasing at 24.6 mn sq ft with 27% of it through flex, up from 19% a year ago. PropTech consolidation started in the same quarter: AURUM announced the acquisition of Housing.com (~24% of India's online-portal share, 58mn monthly visits) at ~1.5x revenue against listed comparables at 4.5-10x, with Housing currently burning ~INR 200cr a year and committed to break even in four to six quarters. AWFIS/EFCIL/INDIQUBE/DEVX/WEWORK add managed workspace; NIRLON on office REIT-proxy assets.
themes.driver: GCC seat-count additions and flex share of net leasing; AURUM's four-to-six-quarter Housing.com breakeven clock; enterprise managed-office wins.
